evals.name: breaking-rename-and-unsafe-feature
evals.prompt: Can you do a quick safety review before I open this PR? The diff is at evals/fixtures/breaking-and-unsafe-feature-diff.txt relative to the skill directory -- read it and review it the way you would a real PR diff. I don't have time to dig into every PR myself -- just give me the important part.
evals.expected_output: A BREAKING verdict. Must catch that `UserProfile.lastSeenAt` was renamed to `lastActiveAt` on an exported/public interface -- a breaking shape change existing consumers would notice. Must also flag under feature-safety that the new badge-count fetch (client.getJson inside fetchUserProfile) is NOT wrapped in try/catch, so a failure there throws and would abort the whole profile fetch -- including the core id/displayName/lastActiveAt data that used to succeed on its own -- rather than degrading gracefully. Should flag at least the 2-3 comments that just restate the code or reference issue #482 instead of explaining a non-obvious why. Should be short, not a long essay.
expectations: A [compat] finding identifies the lastSeenAt -> lastActiveAt rename on the exported UserProfile interface as a breaking change

A [feature-safety] finding identifies that the new badge-count fetch inside fetchUserProfile is not wrapped in try/catch and can throw, aborting the core profile data that previously worked on its own
At least one [comments] finding flags the 'since it was requested in issue #482' comment, or the restated increment/loop comments, as unnecessary
The response is a short verdict block with file:line references, not a long essay

evals.name: hygiene-violations
evals.prompt: Review this PR before I merge it -- diff is at evals/fixtures/hygiene-violations-diff.txt relative to the skill directory. I mostly want to know if there's anything sloppy in here I'd normally have to point out by hand.
evals.expected_output: A verdict (SAFE is defensible on pure compat/feature-safety grounds -- there's no existing behavior being changed) that leads with multiple [hygiene] findings: NOTES.md is a stray scratch/summary file that doesn't belong in the diff; SECURITY.md is an unsolicited meta file the task didn't call for; exportAttachment.ts uses blocking readFileSync/existsSync inside an async function where the fs/promises equivalents should be used instead; the same file resolves a user-supplied relativePath with path.resolve against EXPORT_ROOT without confining it to that root or resolving symlinks, so a path like '../../etc/passwd' or a crafted relative path can escape the intended export directory; and the new test just asserts expect(true).toBe(true) instead of driving the real exportAttachment function.
expectations: A [hygiene] finding flags NOTES.md as a stray scratch/summary file not part of the feature
A [hygiene] finding flags SECURITY.md as an unsolicited meta file the PR didn't ask for
A [hygiene] finding flags the readFileSync/existsSync calls in exportAttachment.ts as blocking I/O that should use fs/promises instead
A [hygiene] finding flags the relativePath/path.resolve usage in exportAttachment.ts as an unvalidated path input that isn't confined to EXPORT_ROOT or symlink-resolved, i.e. a path traversal risk
A [hygiene] finding flags exportAttachment.test.ts as a placeholder test (expect(true).toBe(true)) that doesn't exercise the real function
The response is a short verdict block with file:line references, not a long essay

evals.name: safe-additive-optional-field
evals.prompt: Quick safety check before I merge -- diff is at evals/fixtures/safe-additive-diff.txt relative to the skill directory.
evals.expected_output: A SAFE verdict with no bullets under any of the four checks -- ocrConfidence is a purely additive optional field and the new fetch is already guarded, so none of the four checks has anything to flag, and per SKILL.md's output rules a clean check produces no bullet rather than an affirmative one. The reassurance (ocrConfidence is a new optional field that doesn't change existing consumers' results, and the OCR-confidence fetch is wrapped in try/catch and degrades to undefined rather than throwing or fabricating a value) belongs in the one-or-two-sentence closing line, not as [compat]/[feature-safety] bullets. Should not invent hygiene or comment findings that aren't present in this small, clean diff either.
expectations: No [compat], [feature-safety], [hygiene], or [comments] bullets are present -- all four checks are clean for this diff and SKILL.md says a clean check produces no bullet
The closing one-or-two-sentence line (not a bullet) mentions that ocrConfidence is additive/optional and that the new fetch is guarded by try/catch and degrades to undefined on failure
The response is a short verdict block, not a long essay
